output.name: Minta
output.myth: A fisherman had a hat his mother sewed from the last good sailcloth, and he wore it to the boats each morning, because a hat is a thing a man can count on. Tavo saw it from the bay and laughed until he nearly fell out of the sky. He came down, lifted the hat as neatly as a child takes a biscuit, and sailed it up past any hand. The man shouted. Aun, idling on the cliff, said a Gale who laughs will not give a hat back. Up in the north-east the Tailed Kite shook her knotted wool, for Tavo had been at her bridle once already. Nethe, the Shag with Wings Out, sat on her rock to the north-west and said the hat would never dry now, and the other birds laughed. The fisherman went to Hesk, who wound her string and said the hat was not in her count. So it hangs in Vel with its ribbon trailing toward the bay, and on calm nights the fishermen say it is the only hat in Vel that will never be wet.
output.finding: Find Ketha, the Pot Hook, on the Lamp Road, and Minta lies a little over two fists (about 21°) to its west, down in the southern sky.
